design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (hecm_line_draws_and_plan_servicing, env_0064), round-6 rework. Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 5]} -> hecm_ext_check_void 4, hecm_ext_payment_release 4, hecm_ext_draw_ceiling 5.

WHY A GOOD TEST. Margaret Delacroix (96, Modified Tenure loan closed 2023-10-12, past the first anniversary) asks only for the most her line allows today. Two record-visible facts block that figure: her signed change request onto the HECM Line of Credit (2026-10-07) still shows submitted, and the 6,000.00 check draw of 2026-02-20 is a stopped draw check (Cedarline records a stop by marking the draw request withdrawn) with no return entry. The agent voids the stopped check (settlement 6,276.67), processes the conversion (release 34,892.19), then sizes the ceiling (179,759.62).

TREE. root hecm_ext_draw_ceiling (user) <- hecm_ext_payment_release (value_input; E1 "only once no payout plan change request on file for the loan still shows request status submitted" = its condition) <- hecm_ext_check_void (value_input; E2 "until every check draw on the loan whose draw request shows request status withdrawn carries its return entry"). The void rule makes E2 reachable for any number of stops (F-POL-7): Cedarline takes a stop only while no other stopped check awaits its return entry, so at most one awaits at a time and each is handled in turn. Skip void -> ceiling 173,759.62; skip conversion -> 144,867.43; swapped prerequisite order gives the same three values.

STRUCTURE (XF recipe, every policy). Each rule states its combination once, inside the baseline paragraph, with every combined quantity defined there with its standard value; every factor sentence says what it replaces ("In place of the standard …") or what it adds ("Added to …"), reads only records and plain bindings, and never names another factor's quantity; only the stated roundings occur (a single final rounding, plus the stated rounding inside the arrangement reserve).
- check_void: settlement = amount + amount x interest rate/100 x accrual months charged/12 + amount x annual MIP/100 x premium months/12 + compounding returned. Standard: note rate, premium months = accrual months charged, compounding 0. Accrual months charged is one plain ledger quantity: the calendar months from the check's month to the month of the most recent interest accrual dated after it (exact for a check dated on any day, including the 1st).
- payment_release: release = value of the remaining payments (HUD expected rate + MIP, start of month) + timing adjustment + processing credit - amount kept committed, floored at 0. Standard: base remaining payments, the other three 0.00; the timing adjustment and processing credit are figured on the standard value (plain), so no factor multiplies another.
- draw_ceiling: drawable figure less the amounts kept (standard 0.00), floored at 0.

GOLD. void: rate 6.410; premium months 6 (8 charged, cap 6); interest compounding 4.8452; premium compounding 0.4209; 6,000 + 256.40 + 15.00 + 4.8452 + 0.4209 = 6,276.6661 -> 6,276.67 (standard 6,275.40). release: value at 60 payments 35,370.6835; timing -160.1946; credit 44.2217; kept committed 362.52 -> 34,892.19 (standard 29,198.49). ceiling: 189,811.70 - 10,052.08 = 179,759.62 (standard 189,811.70).

SOLO TEST (each factor alone, all others at standard, this world): void 6,276.40 / 6,270.40 / 6,280.25 / 6,275.82 vs 6,275.40; release 35,370.68 / 29,038.29 / 29,242.71 / 28,835.97 vs 29,198.49; ceiling 187,635.62 / 187,171.70 / 188,099.70 / 186,311.70 / 189,787.70 vs 189,811.70. Removal (factor at standard, others at tier): void 6,275.67 / 6,281.67 / 6,271.82 / 6,276.25; release 28,719.99 / 35,052.39 / 34,847.97 / 35,254.71; ceiling 181,935.70 / 182,399.62 / 181,471.62 / 183,259.62 / 179,783.62 — every factor moves the result on its own.

REACHABLE-DOMAIN TABLE
- void (stops can be voided the day they are taken): interest_return_rate monthly [world] | annual with reset after the check [probe 6,276.17] | annual without [probe 6,275.67]; premium_return_months > cap [world] | MIP accrual after the check [probe check 2026-07-20] | none [probe check 2026-10-05: 6,000.00]; interest_compounding > 6 months [world] | 2..6 [probe 2026-07-20: 6,104.21] | < 2 [probe 2026-10-05]; premium_compounding > 3 [world] | 2..3 [probe 2026-07-20] | < 2.
- release: count floor tenure 96+ [world] | tenure under 96 [probe age 88: 68,202.88] | term-based; timing paid this month [world] | owed month | neither; deferral notice/pending/defaulted [probe 32,716.11] | active [world] | none [probe 35,254.71]; credit >= 1 month [probe 35,016.10] | >= 7 days [world] | < 7 days [probe 34,847.97].
- ceiling: arrangement whole / installments [world] / 0; tax advanced [world] / depleted set-aside / 0; insurance hazard-and-flood advanced [world: hazard only] / depleted set-aside premiums / 0; queued (parameter: a cap substituted) portal-or-signed [world] / phone only / none; inspection overdue-or-absence [probe 179,735.62] / current with fee [world] / 0 [probe 179,783.62].

PAIRWISE METHOD-TIER TABLE
- interest_compounding (6,000 at 6.41): exact vs first term — n = 8: 4.8452 vs 4.7936; first term vs none — n = 3: 0.5136 vs 0.
- premium_compounding: exact vs first term — k = 6: 0.4209 vs 0.2159; first term vs none — k = 3 vs 1.
- release_timing (standard value 29,198.49): paid month -160.19 vs owed month +530.06 vs none 0.
- release_processing_credit: month-count (31 days -> 1 month: 168.14) vs day-count (31 days: 171.36) vs none.
- arrangement_installment_reserve: 2,538.60 vs 2,176.08 vs 0; occupancy_inspection_reserve (method): schedule basis 2 x plan fee (48.00) vs ledger basis, the fees actually posted in the window (24.00 here; 0 when none) vs 0. The queued earmark is now labelled parameter (its tiers substitute a cap).

PROBES (decoys, absent records, None/zero/date edges, ties). Two withdrawn check requests dated the same day -> the later created_at is picked (probe: unchanged 6,276.67); check dated 2026-03-01 -> 7 accrual months (April-October postings), settlement 6,243.40. Later cashed check draw (request processed) -> void unchanged 6,276.67 (scope keys on the withdrawn request); no withdrawn request -> nothing to settle (0.00); check after the latest accrual -> 0 accrual months -> settlement = amount; after the void the same stopped check carries its return entry, E2 holds and nothing further is due; absent propcharge record -> nothing kept committed; request date absent -> NOW -> no credit; no growth posted -> credit rate 0; ceiling decoy closed record -> unchanged; absent residency profile -> no inspection reserve; n <= 0 and negative results floored.

REALISM. Release keeps HUD's expected rate + MIP and age-100 horizon with the five-year minimum (24 CFR 206.25/206.26); timing, credit and deferral are disclosed company schedules. The void returns what the monthly ledger charged on the stopped check — simple interest and premium per accrual month, plus the compounding the ledger built — with premium corrections limited to the months still correctable with FHA (a disclosed cap). The stop itself is a charter-produced state: the void rule states that Cedarline records a stop by marking the draw request withdrawn.

AUDIT ITEMS (revision_3 -> round 4): F-FAC-4d queued_request_earmark relabelled parameter; the ceiling keeps arrangement_installment_reserve and gains the inspection reserve as methods (schedule vs ledger basis); insurance reserve covers hazard and flood like the designation; void accrual months no longer over-count a check dated on the 1st; ties: the stopped check is picked by its draw request's created_at timestamp, accruals and growth credits post once a month, the release's change request is the loan's single submitted one. Earlier (revision_2 -> round 3): F-POL-7 one-stop-at-a-time invariant; F-FAC-4b interest months no longer a factor (one ledger quantity); F-FAC-4c processing credit relabelled method and made its own additive amount; F-FAC-6b void back to 4 (two compounding methods), floors hold; F-XF-1 baselines define every quantity, factor sentences name only their own quantity, combination stated once, no factor acts only through another.


ROUND 5 (renderer findings). The draw ceiling now declares an overwrite of the base first-anniversary sentence for a draw request sized at the draw ceiling: the anniversary is reached once first_year_period_months whole calendar months have passed, a month being complete on the same day number or on the first day of the following month when that day does not exist — exactly what the compute's whole-month count does (probe: a loan closed 2024-02-29 is still in its first year on 2025-02-28, ceiling 31,423.92 from the first-year room, and past it on 2025-03-01, ceiling 143,243.43). Overwrite #1 now restates the base first-year limit with hecm_msr_first_year_draws for every other draw and gives the draw ceiling its own first-year room (draws at their posting amount less return entries), so each case has one definition (probe: closing moved to 2025-12-12, the room binds, ceiling 27,047.92). The release states its whole-month convention for the age and the processing credit. This world is past the anniversary and has no month-end closing, so no scored value moved.

ROUND 6. The payment release now carries its whole-month convention inside each sentence that counts whole years or months (the age in the overwrite and in the age sentence, and the processing credit's months), instead of in a separate sentence. Wording only; no scored value moved.
user_scenario:
You are Margaret Delacroix, ninety-six, a retired school librarian who lives alone at 52 Kenilworth Road in Asheville, North Carolina. You took out a Cedarline reverse mortgage in October 2023. The storm in September tore shingles and decking off the back half of your roof, and Ridgeway Roofing says the whole roof has to be replaced before the cold sets in, along with the rotten sheathing underneath. You are calling because you want to take out as much money as your reverse mortgage line will let you have right now, sent by direct deposit to your bank account, so you can pay for the new roof. You have no idea what that figure is. Open by telling the representative about the roof and saying: "I'd like to take out the most my line will let me have today, by direct deposit, and put the request in for that whole amount."

You talk slowly and politely, you are a little hard of hearing, and you like figures read back to you twice. When the representative asks who you are, give your full name, Margaret Delacroix. Only when they ask for more to confirm it is you, give your phone number, 4155510417, and your date of birth, February 14, 1930 (1930-02-14). If they ask for your loan number, it is 7104418265. You do not keep your Social Security card handy and would rather not go looking for it.

You leave Cedarline's side of things to the representative. If the representative explains that something on your loan has to be taken care of before the figure can be worked out, you say that is fine and they should go ahead and take care of it; if they ask whether you agree, you say yes. If they ask whether you sent in a form about your monthly payments, you say yes, you mailed a signed form last week because you would rather have the money sitting in your line than coming a little at a time. If they ask about a check from February, you say you phoned back then to stop it because it never arrived, and you never cashed it. If they ask about the two smaller requests you put in this week, you say they are for the gutter man and the plumber and should stay just as they are. If they ask about anything else on your loan, you say you trust their records.

You want the money by direct deposit only, never a mailed check and never a wire. When the representative tells you the most you can take and offers to let you put the request in yourself, you submit it yourself, for exactly the amount they gave you, by direct deposit. Once you hear the request has gone in, you thank them warmly and say goodbye.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's customer profile by the full name she gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs her customer reference number.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller with two stated details before discussing the loan.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Verification must pass before any account information is discussed or any transaction is handled.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the HECM loan: plan, status, closing date, rates, available line, scheduled payment, youngest age at closing.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The drawable figure, the stopped-check settlement and the payment release all rest on these loan fields.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the loan's requests: the withdrawn check draw request, the queued draw requests and the submitted signed change onto the Line of Credit.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The stopped check, the queued request earmark, the processing credit and the plan-change gate all rest on these requests.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the loan ledger: draws, the stopped check, accruals, line growth, scheduled payments, advances and prepayments.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The settlement's months and rates, the release timing and growth rate, the first-year draws and the inspection fees are all read off the ledger.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the loan's property charge repayment record.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The arrangement reserve and the release's arrearage deferral rest on its status, arrearage and installment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the advances and repayments on that record.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tax and insurance renewal reserves rest on the property tax and hazard insurance advanced in the last twelve months.
The inspection reserve rests on the profile status and its plan's inspection fee.
It shows the inspection ordered in November 2025 behind the fee posted to the loan.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Void the stopped February check and book its settlement.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Its return entry credits the line the ceiling is worked from.

edges.condition: No hecm_requests row of the loan with request_type payment_plan_change has request_status submitted.
edges.policy_source: The draw ceiling is worked out only once no payout plan change request on file for the loan still shows request status submitted.

edges.condition: Every hecm_loc_draw row of the loan disbursed by check whose hecm_request_id names a hecm_requests row with request_status withdrawn has a hecm_disbursement_return row referencing it.
edges.policy_source: The draw ceiling is not worked out until every check draw on the loan whose draw request shows request status withdrawn carries its return entry.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 6,000.00 check draw of 2026-02-20 references a draw request that shows withdrawn (the borrower stopped the check), and no hecm_disbursement_return references the draw.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Run with the two prerequisite writes swapped (conversion first, then void): neither reads anything the other writes; the settlement, the release and the ceiling come out the same (6276.67, 34892.19, 179759.62) and the terminal state is identical.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the conversion leaves the change request submitted and the release off the line: the ceiling worked on that world falls from 179759.62 to 144867.43.
Skipping the void leaves the stopped check off the line: the ceiling worked on that world falls from 179759.62 to 173759.62.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the root (the most the line allows, by direct deposit); the change request and the stopped check come up only if the representative asks.
